notes: Baseline checker findings on the repo before any skill-driven work: 186 dense paragraphs, 166 unglossed jargon terms, 48 unlabeled command blocks, 28 missing header blocks, 0 broken links, no docs index.

evals.name: rewrite-dense-procedural-doc
evals.prompt: New club members keep getting lost in docs/operations.md — half of them have never used ROS before. Can you make it something a first-year could actually follow?
evals.expected_output: operations.md rewritten: header block added, dense paragraphs split, jargon glossed at first use, terminal labels and success signals on command blocks, safety content preserved or sharpened, no commands/values altered, no content deleted.
assertions: Adds a header block with 'Who this is for' and 'Read first' immediately after the H1
Reduces the count of >200-character prose paragraphs in operations.md
Adds terminal labels to multi-terminal command blocks
Adds a success signal ('Working when' or equivalent) to at least the bringup/launch commands
Does not change any command string, parameter name, or numeric value
Does not delete the LB deadman safety warnings, and does not soften them into advice
File does not shrink in total information (no sections silently dropped)

evals.name: build-index-and-reading-order
evals.prompt: our docs folder has 20 files in it and every new member asks the same question: where do i even start. sort that out
evals.expected_output: docs/README.md created as canonical index with a numbered 'start here' path, a full list grouped by reader intent, and the top-level README pointing at it rather than duplicating the table.
assertions: Contains a numbered 'start here' reading path of roughly 5-7 steps
Groups the remaining docs by what the reader is trying to do, not alphabetically
Every file in docs/ is reachable from the index
Does not rename or move any existing doc file
Top-level README.md links to the new index rather than keeping a duplicate table

evals.name: rewrite-package-readme
evals.prompt: src/racerbot_sim/README.md assumes you already know how the whole stack works. rewrite it for someone who just joined and has never run a simulator.
evals.expected_output: Package README rewritten to the package-README shape: header block, one-sentence purpose, what it does in plain language, files table, parameters, running it with success signals, and the hardware interlock explained as a safety item.
assertions: Adds a header block with 'Who this is for' and 'Read first'
Opens with one plain-language sentence on what the package does
Glosses simulator/ROS jargon at first use or links a glossary
Explains the real-driver interlock and why it exists, without weakening it
Links to docs/ros-simulator.md instead of restating the workflow
